name: Rite of Vision
summary: Baine Bloodhoof sends travelers across Mulgore to seek Zarlman Two-Moons before the Rite of Vision. The trial belongs to the Rites of the Earthmother, and elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff regard it as a sign of spiritual readiness.

sections.title: A Sacred Stepping Stone
sections.body: For generations, the nomadic tauren have followed the Earthmother’s guidance across Kalimdor’s plains. Now they have gathered within Mulgore’s safe borders, where spiritual traditions remain at the heart of their society. Earlier trials test an initiate’s strength and bond with the hunt. The Rite of Vision turns inward, calling young tauren and honored allies to commune with the spirits.

sections.title: The Seer's Guidance
sections.body: Before seeking a vision, an initiate needs guidance in the ancient ways. In Bloodhoof Village, the revered shaman Zarlman Two-Moons offers that counsel. Baine Bloodhoof entrusts travelers to his care. Zarlman recognizes those who walk the ancestors’ path, then gives them the first rites and sacred preparations to look beyond the physical world.

faq.q: What is the Rite of Vision?
faq.answer: The Rite of Vision is a sacred rite of the Earthmother. It opens an adventurer’s spiritual sight, letting them commune with ancestral spirits and show the elders of Thunder Bluff they are spiritually ready.
Baine Bloodhoof sends travelers to undertake the Rite of Vision. The son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof watches over Bloodhoof Village and directs worthy travelers to its spiritual elders.
Zarlman Two-Moons is a seasoned tauren shaman and Bloodhoof Village’s spiritual leader. He prepares travelers and initiates for sacred trials such as the Rite of Vision.

faq.q: Why are the Rites of the Earthmother important to the tauren?
faq.answer: The Rites of the Earthmother mark a traditional passage into adulthood for tauren. Completing them proves physical ability, spiritual attunement, and lasting respect for the land, earning the high elders’ honor.

faq.q: Can non-tauren undertake the Rite of Vision?
aliases: can orcs do rite of vision
faq.answer: Yes. Horde allies passing through Mulgore may follow the Earthmother’s path if they earn the Bloodhoof tribe’s trust. They honor tauren tradition and hope to gain the elders’ favor.

faq.q: Where does this trial take place?
faq.answer: The trial begins in Bloodhoof Village, near the banks of Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore. The village lies south of Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: As a tauren, you reach an essential cultural milestone in the Rite of Vision. It marks your passage toward becoming a trusted defender and spirit-walker of the tribes.
As a shaman, seeking Zarlman Two-Moons and walking the path of visions speaks to your duty to balance worldly affairs with the ancestors’ will.
As a druid, communing with the Earthmother’s visions deepens your calling to hear the wisdom and whispers of the living world.
As a member of the Horde, undertaking these sacred traditions shows your loyalty and respect for the tauren elders who help guide the Horde.
